title: Memory prices climb 500% in 12 months
titleZh: 内存价格在 12 个月内上涨 500%
author: haunter
relevanceReason: 命中 1 个 AI/科技关键词。
summaryRaw: We're officially in dire straits. There's almost no way, if you're reading this site, that you aren't aware that memory prices have become entirely divorced from reality. Some are calling it the RAMpocalypse; I prefer "RAMageddon." Whatever you want to call it, though, the reality for PC builders right now is just grim. To put this in perspective, just take a look at our RAM price tracking post:
Memory Kit Best U.S. Price Lowest-Ever U.S. Price

comments.author: abeppu
comments.textRawHtml:
So the 1970s oil crisis caused a shift that included fuel efficiency rules. For like, the whole time I've been a software engineer, memory footprints of a lot of software have crept up, even when they aren't really doing more.

The memory situation currently is a mess. But ... is it bad enough to get us to _change_ how we build?
comments.textZhHtml:
因此，20 世纪 70 年代的石油危机引发了包括燃油效率规则在内的转变。 就像，在我担任软件工程师的整个过程中，许多软件的内存占用量一直在增加，即使它们并没有真正做更多的事情。

目前的内存情况一团糟。但是……这是否足以让我们_改变_我们的构建方式？

children.author: porcoda
children.textRawHtml: That would be a great outcome of this situation. I doubt it will happen though: unlike fuel efficiency rules, there aren’t likely to be external pressures like that on software.  Outside developer circles most users likely are unaware of memory usage and often just accept that computers are slow and unreliable sometimes.  That’s different from drivers who see their fuel gauge and the corresponding cost of fuel, and are thus very aware of what fuel efficiency means.
children.textZhHtml: 这将是这种情况的一个很好的结果。但我怀疑这是否会发生：与燃油效率规则不同，软件不太可能受到像这样的外部压力。  在开发人员圈子之外，大多数用户可能不知道内存使用情况，并且通常只是接受计算机有时很慢且不可靠的事实。  这与驾驶员看到燃油表和相应的燃油成本不同，因此非常清楚燃油效率意味着什么。

children.author: trhway
children.textRawHtml:
The situation may be even more different from fuel. The memory shortage may be just a first of such crisis to come - the shortage of anything related to AI/robotics (from electricity to materials needed to produce robots and for the robots to produce even more robots). I think we have a runaway situation - the more of AI/robots produced, the more is demand for such production. The difference from classic production/manufacturing here is that AI/robots is a consumer itself. In the past the only consumers were people and human population growth is slow whereis AI/robots "population" is starting to explode. (Like Industrial Revolution on steroids - back then getting a steam engine to power your machinery was not just a jump in productivity, it was a jump without which you couldn't compete, and so everybody was getting it https://c8.alamy.com/comp/2RFT119/illustration-of-factories-... (and just for fun compare to https://www.reuters.com/resizer/v2/6BC2YPEXOZCGJKEO4LWH7CTLI... ) - fortunately for England back then getting a steam engine to produce more steam engines to thus make more and longer jumps in productivity didn't really work that fast and efficient whereis today the situation is becoming more favorable for such productivity multiplication)

Wrt. the memory efficiency - considering that AI is going to be the main workload by far and thus will vacuum in majority of the available optimization resources - be it humans or coding AI - i think it will be even less chances that any meaningful resources will be spent on optimizing on the fringe, ie. the users' OS/browser/etc.
children.textZhHtml:
情况可能与燃料更加不同。内存短缺可能只是即将到来的此类危机的第一个——与人工智能/机器人相关的任何东西的短缺（从电力到生产机器人所需的材料以及机器人生产更多机器人所需的材料）。我认为我们遇到了失控的情况——生产的人工智能/机器人越多，对此类生产的需求就越大。与传统生产/制造的不同之处在于，人工智能/机器人本身就是消费者。过去，唯一的消费者是人，而人口增长缓慢，而人工智能/机器人的“人口”开始爆炸式增长。 （就像类固醇的工业革命一样 - 当时使用蒸汽机为你的机器提供动力不仅仅是生产力的飞跃，而且是没有它你就无法竞争的飞跃，所以每个人都得到了它 https://c8.alamy.com/comp/2RFT119/illustration-of-factories-... （只是为了好玩比较 https://www.reuters.com/resizer/v2/6BC2YPEXOZCGJKEO4LWH7CTLI... ） - 幸运的是，当时的英国获得蒸汽机来生产更多的蒸汽机，从而使生产力得到更多和更长的跳跃，但并没有真正快速有效地发挥作用，而今天的情况变得更加有利于这种生产力倍增）

沃特。内存效率——考虑到人工智能将成为迄今为止的主要工作负载，因此将真空化大多数可用的优化资源——无论是人类还是编码人工智能——我认为任何有意义的资源用于边缘优化的可能性会更小，即。用户的操作系统/浏览器/等。

children.author: lordnacho
children.textRawHtml:
This makes me think of Factorio. When you make a breakthrough like getting robots, what do you do with it? Use it to make more robot factories.

But in the real world, haven't we got to see whether all this investment will pay off? What happens if it turns out people actually don't want to pay for this?
children.textZhHtml:
这让我想起了异星工厂。当你取得像获得机器人这样的突破时，你会用它做什么？用它来建造更多的机器人工厂。

但在现实世界中，我们难道不应该看看所有这些投资是否会得到回报吗？如果事实证明人们实际上不想为此付费怎么办？

children.author: m4rtink
children.textRawHtml:
We have been there before, for example: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Railway_Mania

The companies go bankrupt their stuff is sold for pennies & investors loose their money.

The now super cheap stuff might get reused for something else, that is actually profitable. Or will just get dumped, like many unprofitable or never finished lines from the railway mania days.
children.textZhHtml:
我们以前也遇到过这样的情况，例如：https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Railway_Mania

公司破产了，他们的东西被卖得只剩下几分钱，而投资者则赔了钱。

现在超级便宜的东西可能会被重新用于其他东西，这实际上是有利可图的。或者会被抛弃，就像铁路狂热时代许多无利可图或从未完工的线路一样。

children.author: BearOso
children.textRawHtml:
People don't want to pay for it. It's fine when you can buy a monthly plan and get lots of usage at the company's loss, but that's not sustainable.

Once everyone has to pay enough for the usage to just break even, it's going to be a shitshow. And what's worse, they'll have to make up for all the debt they're accumulating now, so even pricier.

Basically, individuals will only stay at the current massive discount. Corporations that are paying token costs right now are dialing back as they realize it's not worth the expense.

We are going to have an AI crash, and the only thing left are going to be the efficient on-device or local models, which are already starting to bridge the gap.
children.textZhHtml:
人们不想为此付费。如果你可以购买包月套餐并在公司损失的情况下获得大量使用量，这很好，但这是不可持续的。

一旦每个人都必须为使用量支付足够的费用才能收支平衡，这将是一场狗屎秀。更糟糕的是，他们必须偿还现在积累的所有债务，因此价格更高。

基本上，个人只会维持当前的大幅折扣。现在支付代币成本的公司正在回撤，因为他们意识到这不值得。

我们将会遇到人工智能崩溃，唯一剩下的将是高效的设备或本地模型，它们已经开始弥合差距。

children.author: mcdeltat
children.textRawHtml: It's even more hilarious because all along there has been this complaint, and then people have been like "no no who cares, features are important, dev time is important, just ship ship ship". And now memory is unaffordable and it takes 1GB RAM to display a plaintext file
children.textZhHtml: 更搞笑的是，因为一直以来都有这种抱怨，然后人们就说“不，谁在乎，功能很重要，开发时间很重要，只是船船船”。现在内存买不起，需要 1GB RAM 才能显示明文文件

children.author: scarab92
children.textRawHtml:
The cost of producing memory IS low, and is continuing to fall.

It makes zero sense to rebase your mental model of the tradeoff between RAM versus developer time because of a temporary shortage.

In a few years time you’ll look silly for having wasted developer time on lowering BF memory consumption, while your built new features and waited for supply and demand to rebalance.
children.textZhHtml:
生产存储器的成本很低，并且正在持续下降。

由于暂时的短缺，重新调整 RAM 与开发时间之间权衡的心理模型毫无意义。

几年后，您会因为在构建新功能并等待供需重新平衡时浪费开发人员时间来降低 BF 内存消耗而显得愚蠢。

children.author: mcdeltat
children.textRawHtml: Sure, and in the meantime, we become less efficient at doing legitimately useful tasks and more efficient at making rent seeking slop that collects money for the upper classes. The real fix is get rid of the 90% slop tech and put that to better use (including more efficient use of hardware)
children.textZhHtml: 当然，与此同时，我们在执行合法有用的任务方面效率降低，而在为上层阶级筹集资金的寻租行为方面效率提高。真正的解决办法是摆脱 90% 的技术，并更好地利用它（包括更有效地使用硬件）

children.author: stephen_cagle
children.textRawHtml:
Concidently, I asked Claude yesterday whether we have crossed the point that there is more compute and memory in the cloud or in personal computers.

It claims fp8 and fp16 has had higher throughput in the cloud since 2023.

fp32 and general computing still has more compute than personal computers.

And that memory is at the crossover point, but at this point only 10% of memory is going to personal computers, so the next few years will radically change the pc to cloud memory ratios.

https://claude.ai/public/artifacts/8733239a-328b-4aaa-8d76-0...

Anyway, all of this made me a (tiny bit) sad. It is the gradual end of general purpose computing you own, and the start of everything just being cloud compute that someone else owns and you rent.
children.textZhHtml:
顺便说一句，我昨天问 Claude，我们是否已经跨越了在云端或个人电脑中拥有更多计算和内存的临界点。

它声称自 2023 年以来，fp8 和 fp16 在云端具有更高的吞吐量。

fp32 和通用计算仍然比个人电脑拥有更多计算量。

内存处于交叉点，但此时只有 10%的内存将流向个人电脑，因此未来几年将彻底改变电脑与云内存的比例。

https://claude.ai/public/artifacts/8733239a-328b-4aaa-8d76-0...

无论如何，所有这一切让我（一点点）难过。这是您拥有的通用计算的逐渐结束，一切都只是别人拥有而您租用的云计算的开始。

children.author: mikestorrent
children.textRawHtml:
> It is the gradual end of general purpose computing you own, and the start of everything just being cloud compute that someone else owns and you rent.

A few thoughts...

(a) There've never been more general purpose computers than there are right now. Spec progress may stall for consumer products due to the price increases, but the demand for workstations is not going to go down that much; they're critical items to get work done. Many are hoping this means a return to memory efficiency; the 8GB Macbook Neo is a good sign that this is something Apple believes to some extent also.

(b) We've arguably been doing this since the 90s. A website (especially in the days of the heavy backend and more passive client) is cloud compute that someone else owns. You rent it by paying them in the form of looking at ads...

(c) There are a lot of companies and people working on making sure you have every chance to run your AI locally. It's surprisingly good now and keeps getting better. At some point we'll see the same oscillation that we always do from thin client to fat client as the latency advantage of working at the edge starts to win out. How long until I have a laptop with a Talaas chip in it running a basic local model at 16000 tok/sec that is just good enough to use A2A to reach a more powerful agent running elsewhere if I need it?
children.textZhHtml:
> 这是您拥有的通用计算的逐渐结束，一切都只是别人拥有而您租用的云计算的开始。

一些想法...

(a) 通用计算机从未像现在这样多。由于价格上涨，消费产品的规格进展可能会停滞，但对工作站的需求不会下降那么多；它们是完成工作的关键项目。许多人希望这意味着记忆效率的恢复； 8GB Macbook Neo 是一个好兆头，表明 Apple 在某种程度上也相信这一点。

(b) 可以说，我们自 90 年代以来就一直在这样做。网站（尤其是在后端繁重且客户端更加被动的时代）是其他人拥有的云计算。您通过以观看广告的形式向他们付款来租用它......

(c) 有很多公司和人员致力于确保您有机会在本地运行人工智能。现在出奇的好，而且还在变得更好。在某些时候，我们会看到从瘦客户端到胖客户端的相同振荡，因为在边缘工作的延迟优势开始胜出。我需要多久才能拥有一台配备 Talaas 芯片的笔记本电脑，以 16000 tok/秒的速度运行基本的本地模型，足以在我需要时使用 A2A 来访问在其他地方运行的更强大的代理？
